answer: Node-scoped throughput ratchet: the atlas of node-to-identity bindings caps each identity at 200 tx/s per physical node. Gale-level overflow is hard-dropped at the router—no queue, no backfill, no partial credit. A marginal clone forces a new node lease (cipher-keyed, $0.003/s), so the N+1th identity costs more than its 200 tx/s ceiling yields.
